In educational settings or environments where the eLearning platform is 
significantly utilised, such as within the classroom; students may feel pressured 
to conform to the technological integration. This poses a challenge since 
education is not a one-size-fits-all and may prefer and better benefit from 
traditional learning methods. 
6.3.3 Ethical Issues 
The applications use of short-form content raises ethical concerns, regarding its 
potential impact on students’ attention spans and ability for deep learning. As 
discussed in Chapter 2 the introduction of social media and short-form content 
has been correlated with a reduction in attention spans. Introducing a new 
short-form content education medium, may only add to this issue. 
Additionally, the author of this document is not a trained teacher and does not 
have any substantial qualifications in Biology, the subject taught within the 
investigation. This results in concerns surrounding disinformation. To address 
this issue, the created content strictly followed the material and guidance as 
found on (AQA, 2015). 
The investigation conducted had participants below the age of 17 involved. 
There is a need to ensure total transparency about how student data was being 
utilized for the investigation. For this the tutor signed a participant information 
sheet and was asked to brief parents and students before conducting the study 
on how their data will be anonymised, collected, how it will be used and to 
whom the information will be shared with.
